classification.difficultyReason: Form two joining vectors containing an unknown and apply the scalar-multiple condition for parallel vectors.

content.prompt: Given three points $A$, $B$, and $C$ with position vectors $\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}$, $\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}8\\k\end{pmatrix}$ respectively, find the value of $k$ such that $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{BC}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=\begin{pmatrix}8\\k\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\k-7\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
For parallel vectors, the scalar multiple is $1$ because both first components are $3$.
$$\begin{aligned}k-7&=4\\k&=11\end{aligned}$$
